item.title: Mini Crackme: shl+add accumulator check
item.description:
Challenge: rcx holds a pointer to a null-terminated ASCII string (Windows x64 calling convention). Find a string that makes `check` return 1.
check: xor eax, eax ; eax = accumulator xor edx, edx ; edx = index .loop: movzx r8d, byte [rcx+rdx] test r8d, r8d jz .done add eax, r8d ; acc += current byte shl eax, 1 ; acc <<= 1 inc edx jmp .loop .done: cmp eax, 0x188 sete al movzx eax, al ret
Answer: "AB"
Each loop iteration folds a byte into the accumulator with acc = (acc + c) << 1, a base-2 Horner scheme, so later characters get shifted further left than earlier ones. Tracing "AB" (0x41, 0x42): acc=0, then (0+0x41)<<1=0x82, then (0x82+0x42)<<1=0x188, matching the target. Any two-byte string c0 c1 with (c0<<1 + c1)<<1 == 0x188 also passes, so "AB" is one of several valid solutions.
